extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and practitioners preparing or prosecuting reissue patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination, public notice, prosecution, and applicant duties specific to reissue (patent correction) applications, including handling of maintenance fees, priority claims, disclosure duties, protests, and concurrent litigation or PTAB trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees when reissue applications pending or issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees are still due in the original patent if there is at least one pending application for reissue of the original patent. Effective January 16, 2018, separate maintenance fee payments are required for each utility reissue patent during the unexpired part of the term of the original patent (unless the original patent was filed before December 12, 1980).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple reissue patents replace a single original patent (e.g., multiple divisional reissue applications that issue), maintenance fee schedule for the original patent is not altered; however separate maintenance fees are required in each reissue patent. See MPEP § 2504 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: No physical surrender of original patent required
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.178(a), surrender of the patent for which reissue is requested is automatic upon the grant of the reissue patent; physical surrender is not required. Until a reissue application is granted, the original patent shall remain in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to October 21, 2004, physical surrender of the letters patent was required; now the Office may return submitted original letters patent on timely request if readily retrievable from storage, but after issue fee payment a petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) is required to expunge from the file and return the original letters patent. If original letters patent cannot be retrieved or is misplaced, the Office will not create a new one. See MPEP § 1460 for more on surrender and effect of reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim for foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) must be made in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for priority to an earlier foreign filing date under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) must be made in a reissue application, even though such a claim may have been made in the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional certified copy of the foreign application is necessary. For reissue applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the foreign priority information must be presented in an application data sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76. For applications filed prior to that date, the oath or declaration must identify the foreign application per pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63. Examiners should note that foreign priority information on the front page of the patent will not be carried forward to the reissue; examiners should ensure the bibliographic data (bib-data) sheet accurately lists priority and notify applicants of discrepancies (e.g., request corrected ADS under 37 CFR 1.76(c)). See MPEP § 215 and § 214.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing duty to notify Office of prior or concurrent proceedings and material information (37 CFR 1.178(b) and 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any reissue application, the applicant must call to the attention of the Office any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (e.g., interferences, PTAB trials, reexaminations, litigations) and the results of such proceedings. The duty to submit information is continuing from filing until abandonment or issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue applications are subject to the same duty of disclosure as other nonprovisional applications. A person may not execute an oath/declaration unless aware of the duty to disclose all information known to be material to patentability under § 1.56. The Office imposes no responsibility to resubmit all 'References Cited' from the original patent, but applicant must timely apprise the Office of any information material to the claims under consideration in the reissue. Use 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 or file an IDS; see MPEP §§ 1404, 1442.01, 1442.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to file IDS at time of filing reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue applicants are encouraged to file information disclosure statements at the time of filing of the reissue application so that such statements will be available to the public during the 2-month period provided in MPEP § 1441.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 14.11.01 may be used in the first action to remind applicants of duties under 37 CFR 1.178(b) (notify prior/concurrent proceedings) and 37 CFR 1.56 (timely disclose material information). Examiner notes: use in first Office action and insert original patent number in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application files open to the public; Official Gazette announcement (37 CFR 1.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications and related papers in the application file are open to inspection by the public, and copies may be furnished upon payment of the fee. Filing of reissue applications (except CPAs under 37 CFR 1.53(d)) will be announced in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette announcement must include filing date, reissue application and original patent numbers, title, class/subclass, inventor name, owner of record, attorney/agent of record, and examining group/Technology Center. IFW reissue files are available via Patent Center on the USPTO website. Where a 'Notice to File Missing Parts' has been mailed, announcement may be delayed until compliance. Announcement should be before examination; inadvertent failure to publish should be corrected and examination may be delayed two months to allow protests. See MPEP § 1441 and Chapter 1900 for protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination parity with non-reissue nonprovisional applications (37 CFR 1.176)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application will be examined in the same manner as a non-reissue, non-provisional application and is subject to all the rules applicable to non-reissue applications. Reissue applications will be acted on 'special' in advance of other applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An original claim re-presented in reissue will be fully examined as if presented for the first time (except division will not be required). Examination includes compliance with 37 CFR 1.171–1.178 (e.g., reissue oath/declaration compliance per 1.175). Reissue applications with related litigation are acted on immediately, subject to a 2-month delay after publication for protests (MPEP § 1441). Examiner should review original patent file wrapper/file history when examining reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining prior art available in reissue examination (AIA vs pre-AIA considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Available prior art for examination of a reissue application is generally the same as that under which the original application was examined, but in some cases the reissue may be subject to different prior art (AIA vs pre-AIA) depending on the effective filing date of claims in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claim in the reissue application has an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 (first-inventor-to-file) apply to the patent application containing such claim; applications filed before that date are governed by pre-AIA 102/103. Example: benefit claims and effective filing dates can make the entire reissue application subject to AIA provisions or to pre-AIA 102(g). See MPEP §§ 2150 et seq., 2159, and related discussion for how to determine which prior art/statute applies. Also see Grant v. Raymond: reissue claims are treated as if presented in the original patent for effective filing date purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue claims treated as if presented in the original patent for prior art purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims in a reissue application are treated as if they were presented in the patent being reissued for purposes of evaluating patentability over prior art (i.e., as if they had the same effective filing date as the original patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: a reissue patent replaces the original patent and continues the patent privilege. See Grant v. Raymond, 31 U.S. (1832). Note: practical examination prior art availability can still differ where a claim depends on a disclosure with a later effective filing date; see MPEP discussion and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month public delay for examiner action after Official Gazette announcement (37 CFR 1.176)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, a reissue application will not be acted on sooner than 2 months after announcement of the filing in the Official Gazette to allow public review and submission of pertinent information (protests under 37 CFR 1.291(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: the 2-month delay may not be employed in certain circumstances (e.g., continuation or divisional reissue may be acted on sooner). The Office may act without delay upon petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with required fee. Petitions to avoid the 2-month delay (e.g., due to stayed litigation) must clearly identify and justify prompt action. Protestors cannot assume the 2-month delay will always be available. See MPEP § 1441 and § 1901.04 for protests details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests allowed in reissue applications; pre-issuance submissions not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest pursuant to 37 CFR 1.291 may be filed during the pendency of a reissue application (before mailing of a notice of allowance) subject to timing constraints. A pre-issuance submission under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) is not permitted in a reissue application because reissue is a post-issuance proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although reissue applications are announced (published) in the Official Gazette, the 35 U.S.C. 122(c) prohibition on post-publication protests for original applications does not apply to reissue applications. Third-party submissions that would be compliant under 37 CFR 1.290 for original applications will be entered as a protest under 37 CFR 1.291 for reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-period and procedural requirements for filing protests in reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest should generally be filed within the 2-month period following the Official Gazette announcement. A protest filed after a final rejection or after prosecution is closed requires a petition for entry under 37 CFR 1.182; a protest not filed prior to a notice of allowance will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition under 1.182 must explain why additional time was necessary and the nature of the protest; must be served on applicant per 37 CFR 1.248 and filed with the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(f)) before expiration of the 2-month period. Protestors seeking extension of the 2-month period may petition to (A) extend the 2-month period and (B) delay examination until it expires; petitions considered only if timely and justified. For 'REISSUE LITIGATION' protests, file early to be considered when the Office first acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applications taken up 'special' and priority handling
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications are taken up 'special,' and remain special even if applicant does not respond promptly. All reissue applications, except those suspended because of litigation or pending PTAB trial, will be taken up for action ahead of other 'special' applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means issues not deferred will be treated and responded to immediately. Reissue applications involved in litigation will be taken up before other reissue applications. RCEs filed on a reissue application will not be announced in the Official Gazette; CPAs of design reissue applications are not announced either.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reissue applications involving concurrent litigation or PTAB trials
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid duplicative effort, action in reissue applications with an indication of concurrent litigation will generally be suspended sua sponte. The PTAB may suspend action where it has jurisdiction. If any of these apply, the Office may or may not suspend: (A) a stay of the litigation is in effect; (B) litigation or PTAB trial has been terminated; (C) no significant overlapping issues exist; (D) applicant desires examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of (A)-(D) apply, examiner should suspend action and consult the Technology Center Training Quality Assurance Specialist (TQAS) or Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS) before suspending. Form paragraphs (14.08–14.11) may be used to deny or grant suspension and provide standard notices (e.g., 'Action in Reissue Stayed — Related Litigation'). When stayed, extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted; applicants normally given 2 months to reply in reissues examined during or after litigation, with further extension only upon clear justification under 37 CFR 1.136(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to inquire into litigation details and annotate file
rubrics_metrics.description: During initial review, the examiner should determine whether the patent to be reissued is involved in litigation or a pending PTAB trial and, if so, the status; the examiner may inquire for specific details of the litigation in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.06 to request materials; if additional litigation details appear material, make additional inquiries as needed. For PTAB trials, examiner may view status via PTAB electronic file system. If litigation becomes known during examination, check MPEP § 1442.02 to determine whether prosecution should be suspended. For IFW files, annotate printed bib-data sheet to provide notice of litigation or PTAB trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement content when reissue seeks to change inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reissue application seeks to change inventorship of a patent, the names of the inventors of record of the patent file are set forth in the Official Gazette announcement (not the filing receipt), while the filing receipt sets forth the names the reissue application is seeking to make of record upon reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction ensures public notice of current inventorship of the patent being reissued; examiners should verify announcement data matches file contents and advise applicant to correct discrepancies in bib-data as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and disclaimers when previously unclaimed subject matter is presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction between subject matter of the original patent claims and previously unclaimed subject matter may be required (restriction involving only subject matter of the original patent claims will not be required). If restriction is required, the subject matter of the original patent claims will be held to be constructively elected unless a disclaimer of all the patent claims is filed in the reissue application, which disclaimer cannot be withdrawn by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should apply restriction practice analogous to non-reissue applications but note special rules about constructive election and non-withdrawable disclaimers for original claims. See MPEP §§ 1450 and 1451 for further handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination may be subject to different prior art if claims rely on later disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Although reissue claims are usually treated as having the same effective filing date as the original patent, if a newly presented claim in the reissue must rely on a disclosure (e.g., a parent or later application) with a later effective filing date, the reissue application (or the claim) may be subject to different prior art and statutes (e.g., AIA provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in text: a reissue claim that relies on an April 1, 2013 disclosure may render the entire reissue application subject to AIA first-inventor-to-file provisions and pre-AIA 102(g) as applicable. Examiners must analyze effective filing dates and benefit claims carefully (see MPEP §§ 2151–2156 and § 2159.03).
